## Overview

This 2026-09-16 snapshot of a Braintree Node.js website response reference is titled "Samsung Pay Card." Its substantive content is a product-ID reference: the Braintree gateway returns product IDs for credit and debit card payment methods, and the generally one-to-three-character ID indicates the specific credit product issued to the customer. This establishes the documented object label and lookup purpose, not client-wallet behavior, current Samsung Pay availability, merchant or buyer eligibility, or successful payment execution.

The page's "Returned within the following response objects" section contains two blank list items, so this snapshot does not identify any containing response object. It also does not expose a populated property-definition table beyond the product-ID reference.

## Key takeaways

- The page is the exact Node.js website response-reference variant titled "Samsung Pay Card"; it is not SDK-package or GitHub implementation evidence.
- The product-ID section describes gateway-returned identifiers for credit and debit card payment methods and qualifies their usual length as one to three characters.
- The long code/name table is reference inventory; use the raw locator for exact entries rather than treating selected examples as exhaustive.
- An object label or returned identifier is not proof that a wallet is currently available, enabled, eligible, or that a payment executed successfully.
